gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus caps its TT-30R and UPS outlets at 1,440 W of pass-through and leaves its L14-30R 240 V outlet unusable while it runs on 120 V wall power. Anker's own page states both limits.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited in both chats), EnergySage (cited) and TheOutagePlan (cited, but it failed to load with a TLS certificate error, so it was not checked). StormWatts gives only part of this: '240 V output cannot be used while the F3800 Plus is charging via 120 V AC'. It has no 1,440 W pass-through cap and no generator rules: 3,000 W on L1 only from a 120 V generator, under 5% THD required, and the Generator Adapter supports a single F3800 Plus. EnergySage says the F3800 Plus is '120 V and 240 V split-phase' and gives no limits. EnergySage gives part of the Apex 300 point ('2,400 W (more with SolarX 4K)') but never says that BLUETTI's 4,000 W solar figure needs the SolarX 4K add-on.
decides: This confirms the F3800 Plus as the 240 V pick only for shoppers who will feed it from a 240 V generator or from a transfer switch with the Home Power Panel. A shopper who plugs it into a wall outlet gets 1,440 W of 120 V pass-through and no 240 V. The F3800 Plus also shows Sold Out on ankersolix.com today, which hurts it as a pick. For the BLUETTI Apex 300 that ChatGPT showed as a 'solar generator', solar charging at the advertised 4,000 W needs the separately sold SolarX 4K. The page should list that add-on next to the Apex 300 price.

findings.label: Outlets while running on 120 V wall power (no generator)
findings.value: TT-30R and UPS outlets limited to 1,440 W pass-through; L14-30R 240 V outlet unusable
findings.note: From the maker page's input/output scenarios. Page note: 'The 240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC.'

findings.label: Generator input limits
findings.value: 120 V generator: TT-30R up to 3,000 W on L1 only; 240 V generator: TT-30R 3,000 W and L14-30R 6,000 W; generator must be 120 V pure sine wave with THD under 5%
findings.note: Maker page. 'Anker SOLIX Generator Adapter required and only support single F3800 Plus unit.'

findings.label: Generator bypass support by generation
findings.value: Supported on F3800 Plus; not supported on the original F3800
findings.note: Maker page FAQ. The same page says the F3800 and F3800 Plus can share a Home Power Panel, Double Power Hub and transfer switch at the same time.

findings.label: Compatible expansion battery
findings.note: Maker spec. 6 × 3.84 kWh plus the 3.84 kWh unit = 26.88 kWh per host.

findings.label: Rooftop solar during an outage via Home Power Panel
findings.value: Not supported; connect 11–165 V panels directly to the unit (above 165 V 'may cause damage to the solar input ports')

findings.label: Store status
findings.value: Sold Out on ankersolix.com, no price shown ('Price Loading')
findings.note: Our current page shows $2,599.99 from an earlier read. Re-check before publishing.

findings.label: Solar input requirement
findings.value: Up to 4,000 W solar input 'Requires a SolarX 4K'
findings.note: Maker page. The page does not say whether the unit has any built-in solar input without the SolarX 4K.

findings.label: Compatible expansion batteries and scale
findings.value: B300K and B500K; 2–3 units and up to 18 batteries for up to 11.52 kW output and 58 kWh

findings.label: Price
findings.note: BLUETTI US store price on the read date.

findings.label: Home integration
findings.value: Home Backup Kit bundle; with the AT1 panel it powers essential circuits during outages; 0 ms or 20 ms switchover
findings.note: The page does not say which setup gives 0 ms and which gives 20 ms.
